headline: Approved a $36,786,032 school roof bond, a $1,000,000 Forest Park learning center grant, and first steps on a Woodland ordinance.
summary: Council approved a Springfield Fire Chiefs Association contract, several donations and grants, and a utility easement for Gerena School. It referred a change to the Holistic host community agreement to the General Government Committee. Council also approved one-way street changes and new four-way stop signs on Washington Street.
decisions: Approved the Eversource Gas petition for Sherman Street, 11-0.
Approved the Eversource petition for 1400 State Street, 11-0.
Approved the Eversource petition for Barrington Drive, 11-0.
Approved the Zayo petition for Liberty Street, 11-0.
Approved the Zayo petition for Chestnut Street, 11-0.
Approved making Edgewood Street one way, 11-0.
Approved making Sycamore Street one way, 11-0.
Approved four-way stop signs on Washington Street, 11-0.
Approved a $10.00 donation to the Springfield City Library, 11-0.
Approved a $100.00 donation to the Springfield City Library, 11-0.
Approved a $547.00 donation of goods to Elder Affairs, 11-0.
Approved a $1,000 Community Health Equity Survey (CHES) mini grant, 11-0.
Approved a $3,905.17 Anti-Heroin Task Force Program grant with no match required, 11-0.
Approved a $55,775.60 Municipal Road Safety Grant with no match required, 12-0.
Approved a $58,500 Recycling Dividends Program grant with no match, 11-0.
Approved a $125,129.85 FY27 Shine Earmark grant with no match, 12-0.
Approved a $500,000 Economic Development Initiative Community Project Funding grant, 12-0.
Approved a $1,000,000 grant for the Forest Park horticulture and learning center, 12-0.
Approved a $108,078.74 transfer from the cable PEG access account for the Comcast franchise fee, 12-0.
Approved a $1,000,000 transfer from stabilization reserves to the Targeted Tax Relief fund, 12-0.
Approved a $36,786,032 bond to pay for school roof replacement projects, 12-0.
Approved the collective bargaining agreement with the Springfield Fire Chiefs Association, 12-0.
Referred the First Amendment to the Holistic host community agreement to the General Government Committee, 12-0.
Approved the order granting a permanent utility easement at Gerena School, 12-0.
Approved first steps on the Chapter 368 woodland ordinance, 12-0, with further committee discussion requested.
Approved a resolution supporting American International College and its legacy in Springfield, 12-0.
Approved supporting House Bill 4087 on camera enforcement of traffic rules, 11-0 with one abstention.

 26. Amending Chapter 368 — Woodland Ordinance  
COUNCILORS DAVILA AND GOVAN PRESENTED THE ORDINANCE.  ATTORNEY 
KAHN FROM THE LAW DEPARTMENT WAS ALSO PRESENT TO FIELD QUESTIONS. 
 THE COUNCILORS SHOUTED OUT THE TEAM FROM SCANS FOR MOVING THIS 
ORDINANCE FORWARD. 
COUNCILOR SANTANIELLO ASKED FOR CLARIFICATION FROM ATTY KAHN. 
COUNCILOR MARTIN IS IN FAVOR OF THE ORDINANCE. 
COUNCILOR BROWN WHERE DOES THE FEE AMOUNT COME FROM?  THIS MAY BE 
UNAFFORDABLE FOR THE HOMEOWNER. 
COUNCILOR WALSH ECHOED COUNCILOR BROWN'S COMMENT.  $300 SEEMS 
HIGH FOR A FEE. 
COUNCILOR GOVAN CLARIFIED THE FEE SCHEDULE.  ALSO STATED THERE IS 
MONEY FOR ASSISTANCE FOR THE HOMEOWNERS. 
ATTORNEY KAHN MADE CLARIFYING COMMENTS. 
COUNCILOR WHITFIELD THANKED EVERYONE FOR THEIR WORK ON THIS 
ORDINANCE.  SHE WANTED MORE DISCUSSION IN COMMITTEE ON FEES, 
APPEALS PROCESS AND TURNAROUND TIME. 
COUNCILOR WALSH WOULD LIKE TO SPEAK MORE ABOUT THIS ORDINANCE IN 
COMMITTEE. 
COUNCILOR PEREZ PUTS ADDITIONAL BURDENS ON CODE ENFORCEMENT 
WHERE THE CITY IS ALREADY SHORT. 
COUNCILOR FENTON IS HAPPY TO SUPPORT FIRST STEPS THIS EVENING BUT 
ALSO WOULD LIKE TO CONTINUE THE DISCUSSION IN COMMITTEE.

in the City of Springfield

COUNCILOR PEREZ RECEIVED A SCHOLARSHIP TO AIC, SO SHE IS PASSIONATE 
ABOUT THE RESOLUTION. 
COUNCILOR SANTANIELLO STATED THAT CONGRESSIONAL REPRESENTATIVE 
NEAL IS ALUMNI OF AIC AND THAT HE SHOULD BE INVOLVED IN THIS. 
COUNCILOR WALSH IS IN SUPPORT OF THE RESOLUTION, AS SHE HAS HAD 
FAMILY MEMBERS ATTEND THE INSTITUTION. 
COUNCILOR GOVAN SPOKE ABOUT DECREASES IN ENROLLMENT AT ALL LEVELS 
OF EDUCATION. 
COUNCILOR HURST THANKED THE COUNCILORS FOR BRINGING THIS MATTER 
FORWARD. 
 
AYES Brian Santaniello, Gerry Martin, Maria Perez, Malo Brown, Zaida

 30. Supporting House Bill 4087 (09/08/2026) 
TAKEN SECOND OUT OF ORDER WITHOUT OBJECTION.  COUNCILOR CLICK 
BRUCE STATED THAT THERE WAS A SUB COMMITTEE MEETING ON THIS TOPIC. 
 STATE REPRESENTATIVE ORLANDO RAMOS PRESENTED THE HOUSE BILL. 
 STATED THAT THESE ARE NOT FLOCK CAMERAS BUT PICTURE CAMERAS.  THEY 
TAKE PICTURES OF VEHICLES BREAK TRAFFIC RULES. 
COUNCILOR SANTANIELLO HAD A QUESTION ABOUT THE CAMERAS.
COUNCILOR MARTIN STATED THAT WAS A TOPIC IN THE PUBLIC SAFETY 
COMMITTEE. 
COUNCILOR GOVAN STATED THAT THESE ARE SIMILAR TO THE MASS PIKE 
CAMERAS. 
COUNCILOR FENTON IS HAPPY TO SUPPORT THIS BILL. 
COUNCILOR PEREZ WANTED TO KNOW HOW MANY CAMERAS AND WHERE.  THIS 
WOULD BE UP TO THE CITY COUNCIL. 
COUNCILOR HURST SUPPORTS THIS HOUSE BILL. 
COUNCILOR DAVILA ALSO THANKED THE REPRESENTATIVES AND IS IN SUPPORT 
OF THE BILL. 
 
AYES Brian Santaniello, Gerry Martin, Maria Perez, Zaida Govan, Kateri 
Walsh, Justin Hurst, Victor Davila, Michael Fenton, Lavar Click-
